beats.visual: A small fish near a shallow shoreline lifts its head above water and gulps air while bubbles trail behind it.
beats.purpose: show that air breathing can help a fish get oxygen outside water
beats.visual_fingerprint: single shoreline fish breaking the surface at water edge, upward head action, close vertical composition with rippling blue water and warm sunlight
beats.continuity: first body image establishes the adaptation world

beats.visual: The same type of fish swims between water and a muddy bank, with its wet body partly supported by the shallow pool.
beats.purpose: show that breathing air does not remove the need for a watery environment
beats.visual_fingerprint: fish half-submerged in a muddy shoreline pool, side view showing wet skin and surrounding water plants, medium shot
beats.continuity: same shoreline world, shifted from surface breathing to habitat dependence

beats.narration_slice: Its body must handle dry ground.
beats.visual: A fish rests on damp earth beside a puddle, showing the challenge of supporting its body away from water.
beats.purpose: show the physical challenge of surviving on land
beats.visual_fingerprint: fish on muddy ground beside a shrinking puddle, low angle view emphasizing body weight and dry surroundings
beats.continuity: moves from water dependence to the land challenge

beats.narration_slice: Its fins must support land movement.
beats.visual: Close view of a fish using sturdy fin movements against wet sand near the shore, with fin structure clearly visible.
beats.purpose: show that fins would need changes for movement on land
beats.visual_fingerprint: close-up fin action on sandy shoreline, angled top-down composition focused on contact between fins and ground
beats.continuity: same shore setting, focusing from whole body problem to a specific adaptation

beats.visual: A colorful group of fish moves through a healthy shallow aquatic habitat with plants, rocks, and flowing water.
beats.purpose: show the many survival benefits provided by water
beats.visual_fingerprint: school of fish in a bright underwater plant-filled zone, wide overhead composition with flowing currents and depth
beats.continuity: expands from one fish challenge to the broader underwater ecosystem

beats.narration_slice: Some fish already use air sometimes.
beats.visual: A mudskipper-like fish climbs on a wet bank beside mangrove roots while taking air from above the water.
beats.purpose: show real fish examples that already use air occasionally
beats.visual_fingerprint: small amphibious fish on mangrove mud, side profile with raised head and exposed roots forming the background
beats.continuity: returns to shoreline to show an existing adaptation example

beats.visual: A scientist observes a fish in a natural shoreline research setting with simple field tools and a magnifying lens.
beats.purpose: show scientific study of fish adaptations
beats.visual_fingerprint: field researcher kneeling beside a shallow stream examining fish habitat, medium-wide composition with natural tools
beats.continuity: moves from animal example to observing and learning about adaptations

beats.narration_slice: A land fish needs many more changes.
beats.visual: A visual comparison in the same crayon world shows a fish silhouette with highlighted areas for body support, fins, and moisture needs without any text labels.
beats.purpose: show that becoming land-adapted requires multiple body changes
beats.visual_fingerprint: single fish centered on split shoreline environment, surrounding visual cues of stronger fins, body support, and wet habitat needs, front-facing composition
beats.continuity: transforms research observation into a clear adaptation explanation

beats.visual: A fish with air-breathing ability returns to the water beside a dry landscape, emphasizing that one feature is not enough for land life.
beats.purpose: show that a single adaptation does not solve every survival challenge
beats.visual_fingerprint: fish at boundary between dry shore and water, wide vertical composition contrasting one useful ability with many environmental demands
beats.continuity: concludes the explanation by connecting all adaptation challenges

beats.narration_slice: Adaptation means changes living things make to survive in a place.
beats.visual: A vibrant shoreline ecosystem shows different fish and plants fitting their environments, with the adapted fish swimming between water and land.
beats.purpose: summarize adaptation as changes that help living things survive in their habitats
beats.visual_fingerprint: full ecosystem view of shoreline with varied organisms in matching habitats, panoramic vertical composition from underwater foreground to sunny bank
beats.continuity: final wide view connects individual fish changes to the whole living world
